stem: Neural Networks: which statement is correct?

options.text: A neural network passes numbers through connected layers.
Every layer stores only words and never numbers.
Training keeps all weights fixed forever.
Adding layers guarantees a correct answer without data.

explanation_after: A neural network passes numbers through connected layers.

stem: Activation Functions: which statement is correct?

options.text: Activation functions let networks learn non-linear rules.
Activations permanently remove the need for weights.
Every activation produces text labels directly.
The same output gate is correct for every possible task.

explanation_after: Activation functions let networks learn non-linear rules.

stem: Forward Propagation: which statement is correct?

options.text: Forward propagation carries inputs through layers to a prediction.
A forward pass updates every weight before producing output.
Batches must contain exactly one example.
Evaluation mode randomly removes more units than training mode.

explanation_after: Forward propagation carries inputs through layers to a prediction.

stem: Loss Functions: which statement is correct?

options.text: Loss is only a chart and never affects training.
Mean squared error fits numeric targets.
The largest possible loss always means the best model.
One loss has the correct meaning for every output type.

explanation_after: Mean squared error fits numeric targets.

stem: Gradient Descent & Optimizers: which statement is correct?

options.text: An optimizer creates training labels from nothing.
Training repeats prediction, loss, gradient, and update steps.
Weights should move in the direction that raises loss.
Momentum deletes all information from earlier steps.

explanation_after: Training repeats prediction, loss, gradient, and update steps.

stem: Training Loops, Epochs & Batches: which statement is correct?

options.text: An epoch is one single number inside a feature.
An epoch is one full pass through the training set.
Validation should secretly train the model.
Larger batches always fit in memory and always improve accuracy.

explanation_after: An epoch is one full pass through the training set.

stem: Learning Rate & Hyperparameters: which statement is correct?

options.text: The learning rate is the model’s final accuracy.
Hyperparameters are always discovered perfectly without experiments.
Schedules can use warmup and later decay.
Warmup begins with the largest possible update.

explanation_after: Schedules can use warmup and later decay.

stem: Overfitting in Deep Networks: which statement is correct?

options.text: Overfitting means both training and validation are always perfect.
Dropout permanently deletes the same units at deployment.
Weight decay discourages large weights.
The test set should guide every training decision.

stem: Batch Normalization: which statement is correct?

options.text: Batch normalization removes every learned parameter.
Evaluation should always use random batch measurements.
Training uses batch statistics.
Normalization guarantees that overfitting cannot occur.

stem: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients: which statement is correct?

options.text: Vanishing gradients make every update infinitely large.
Gradient clipping creates new labels for the dataset.
Depth can never affect backward signal scale.
Initialization helps keep signals in a workable range.

explanation_after: Initialization helps keep signals in a workable range.

stem: CNN Basics: which statement is correct?

options.text: A CNN requires a separate full model for every pixel.
Stride means the number of class labels.
Padding always deletes the image border.
Padding controls border handling and output size.

explanation_after: Padding controls border handling and output size.

stem: RNN Basics: which statement is correct?

options.text: An RNN treats every sequence position as unrelated.
Hidden state is always a human-readable sentence.
Padding should contribute to the training loss as real data.
Masks prevent padded positions from acting like real data.

explanation_after: Masks prevent padded positions from acting like real data.

stem: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs: which statement is correct?

options.text: RNNs can remain useful for streaming or constrained devices.
Transformers read only the immediately previous token.
Parallel training means token order no longer matters.
Attention has zero memory cost at every sequence length.

explanation_after: RNNs can remain useful for streaming or constrained devices.

stem: PyTorch Introduction: which statement is correct?

options.text: Gradients accumulate unless they are cleared.
A tensor can contain only one number.
An nn.Module prevents parameters from being trained.
Autograd requires every derivative to be entered by hand.

explanation_after: Gradients accumulate unless they are cleared.

stem: Build Your First Network: which statement is correct?

options.text: A fresh-process load test verifies the saved artifact.
A model learns merely because its script exits successfully.
Only the final accuracy number is needed to reproduce a run.
Validation rows should be used for every weight update.

explanation_after: A fresh-process load test verifies the saved artifact.

options.text: Backpropagation changes labels before training.
Reverse-mode differentiation is efficient when many parameters lead to one loss.
The backward pass never uses the forward computation.
Every weight receives the same correction.

explanation_after: Reverse-mode differentiation is efficient when many parameters lead to one loss.

stem: Neural Networks: which statement is correct?

options.text: Every layer stores only words and never numbers.
Initialization scale affects whether signals remain usable through deep networks.
Training keeps all weights fixed forever.
Adding layers guarantees a correct answer without data.

explanation_after: Initialization scale affects whether signals remain usable through deep networks.

stem: Activation Functions: which statement is correct?

options.text: Activations permanently remove the need for weights.
An activation’s slope affects how gradients travel backward.
Every activation produces text labels directly.
The same output gate is correct for every possible task.

explanation_after: An activation’s slope affects how gradients travel backward.
